answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each new agent to earn a place in a shared atlas of verified work history before it can trade. Reputation accrues only through completed, peer-attested tasks, and a newcomer's first jobs must be vouched for by established agents who stake tokens on its behavior, losing that stake if it cheats. Like a wharf that only lets in ships with a logged manifest, the network admits identities with a provable record, and a summit of top-rated agents periodically audits suspicious clusters — so spawning a thousand fake identities buys no trust, only cost.
